description: Causal time-series functions for finance and signal processing in C++, for Python (screamer) and JavaScript (@screamer-labs/screamer): rolling statistics, technical indicators, filters, market microstructure, bars from ticks, backtests, and significance tests, with the same results on stored arrays and on a live feed.
rules: Search for an existing screamer function before writing a calculation by hand in numpy or pandas: `python -m screamer.docs search <keywords>`, or `npx screamer-docs search <keywords>` in JavaScript.

Construct a function with its parameters, then call it on data: `RollingMean(window_size=20)(prices)`. The output container follows the input: array in, array out; list in, list out; float in, float out; iterator in, lazy iterator out.
Axis 0 is time: a (T, K) array is K independent series of length T. There is no axis= argument. A list is a series, never a scalar: [4.0] is a series of length 1.
Every function is causal. Do not shift inputs to avoid look-ahead, and do not use backward fills or centered windows. Outputs are NaN until a window is full unless start_policy says otherwise.

Backtest engines take the target position and fill at the next opportunity; do not lag the target yourself. Use position_test for a fixed strategy and strategy_test when the strategy was tuned on the same data.
In JavaScript, call `await ready()` once, then call factories without `new`; options are camelCase (`RollingRSI({ windowSize: 14 })`) and plain functions are camelCase (`positionTest`).
